claim_verdicts.evidence: Design reasoning (kind opinion), now worded with its condition: sec 2 "makes every signed-in request fail while Keycloak is down", q4 explanation c "refuse signed-in requests while Keycloak is down". A per-token call to a server that is down cannot succeed; anonymous endpoints are no longer included. No version-specific behaviour asserted.

Ledger now matches: "until its exp (plus the default clock skew, 300 s, which Program.cs leaves unchanged)". TokenValidationParameters.DefaultClockSkew: "Default for the clock skew." Remarks: "300 seconds (5 minutes)." Program.cs:37-55 sets no ClockSkew. RFC 7519 4.1.4 exp: "the expiration time on or after which the JWT MUST NOT be accepted". Lesson sec 8 "until it expires" is acceptable at this depth.

RFC 7519 sec 8: "only HMAC SHA-256 ("HS256") and "none" MUST be implemented"; "It is RECOMMENDED that implementations also support RSASSA-PKCS1-v1_5 with the SHA-256 hash algorithm ("RS256")". Stage-1 JwtTokenService.cs signs with SecurityAlgorithms.HmacSha256 and one config key. Live Keycloak token header alg RS256; JWKS signing key kty RSA (claims 2, 3 run). Keycloak admin guide: "asymmetric key pairs, a private and public key".
